answer: Submissions that land within 223 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The meadow detector writes to garden, and willow publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 132 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
